reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g2_na_q3_1), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The generated items directly and faithfully fulfill the competency requirement to illustrate and write multiplication as repeated addition across concrete, pictorial, and numeric representations. The items feature repeated addition equations connected directly to multiplication expressions (e.g., "6 + 6 = ___. What is 6 × 2?" and "2 + 2 + 2 = ___. What is 2 × 3?"), counting by multiples (e.g., "Count by 4s: 4, 8, 12. 4 × 3 = ___"), number line models (e.g., "Starting at 0, take 2 equal jumps of 3 on the number line. What is 3 × 2?"), and array representations (e.g., "Look at the 6×2 array. How many squares are shaded in all?").

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set comprehensively covers all representation modalities named in the MATATAG learning competency: equal jumps on a number line (e.g., "Starting at 0, take 5 equal jumps of 8 on the number line. What is 8 × 5?"), counting by multiples (e.g., "Count by 7s: 7, 14. What is 7 × 2?"), arrays and grids (e.g., "Shade 5 rows of 2 squares to show 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2. How many squares did you shade in all?" and "Look at the 2×4 array. It shows 4 + 4. How many squares are shaded in all?"), repeated addition sentences (e.g., "4 + 4 + 4 = ___"), and equal groups in real-world contexts (e.g., "Moses puts 4 baskets in each of 3 bags. How many baskets are in all the bags?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive demand, vocabulary, sentence length, and structural complexity are perfectly tailored to Grade 2 Quarter 3 learners. Items utilize straightforward prompts, clear visual instructions, and accessible scaffolds (e.g., "Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6. 2 × 3 = ___" and "5 + 5 = ___. What is 5 × 2?"), avoiding any over-complicated phrasing or extraneous cognitive load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample set demonstrates excellent format diversity across multiple item types including multiple-choice (e.g., "Starting at 0, take 2 equal jumps of 2 on the number line. What is 2 × 2?"), cloze / fill-in-the-blank (e.g., "4 + 4 + 4 = ___"), true/false evaluations (e.g., "2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. True or False?" and "Starting at 0, taking 5 equal jumps of 7 on the number line lands on 35. True or False?"), visual shading tasks (e.g., "Shade all the squares inside the 8×10 rectangle. How many squares did you shade in all?"), and error detection (e.g., error detection (seed 51: "4 + 4 + 4 = ___")).

competency_alignment.rationale: All items strictly align with the conceptual definition of multiplication as repeated addition without drifting into unrelated domains or higher-grade techniques (such as standard vertical algorithms or formal division). Every item explicitly bridges grouping, skip counting, number lines, or arrays with the foundational multiplication concept (e.g., "Look at the 2×4 array. It shows 4 + 4. How many squares are shaded in all?").

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The scale of factors and products is fully aligned with Grade 2 curriculum standards. Multipliers and group sizes range appropriately from small single-digit factors (e.g., "Starting at 0, take 2 equal jumps of 3 on the number line. What is 3 × 2?") up to manageable multiples of 5, 7, 8, and 10 (e.g., "Shade all the squares inside the 8×10 rectangle. How many squares did you shade in all?"), keeping calculations within the appropriate range of 0 to 100.
